title: A grounded answer workflow
summary: Turn a real decision into bounded claims, trace each claim to suitable evidence, challenge gaps and stale sources, then answer with citations and justified uncertainty.
description: This fictional lesson follows an internal maintenance scheduling decision through question, scope, evidence requirements, source ledger, claim mapping, challenge, and a cited answer. It demonstrates an illustrative evidence-grounding process, not proof that arbitrary generated claims are true.
altText: A native interactive flow has seven nodes: Question, Scope, Requirements, Ledger, Claim map, Challenge, and Answer. The main route proceeds in that order. At Challenge, Missing or weak evidence returns to Ledger, while Supported proceeds to Answer.
caption: Grounded answers require bounded claims, relevant and sufficiently fresh evidence, explicit challenge, traceable citations, and honest uncertainty.
takeaways: Authority, freshness, and relevance are separate source properties. A source can be authoritative yet stale, fresh yet outside the decision scope, or relevant but unable to establish a required claim.
Conflicting extracts should be compared by version date, stated supersession, authority, and scope. Do not merely count sources.
Every decision-bearing claim needs evidence strong enough for that claim. Missing evidence sends the workflow back to the ledger rather than inviting a guess.
A fluent sentence is not supported merely because it is specific or plausible. Its citations must entail its claims.
A cited answer should distinguish established facts, assumptions, unresolved uncertainty, and the narrow decision those facts support.
This workflow illustrates disciplined evidence use. It cannot guarantee that supplied records are authentic, complete, or true, and it does not prove arbitrary generated claims.
textAlternativeLabel: Complete text alternative for every branch
textAlternative: Start at Real question or decision and state the complete decision, date, target, and desired output. Continue to Bound scope and assumptions, where included and excluded systems, time boundaries, and assumptions are explicit. Continue to Define evidence requirements and identify what must be established before answering. Continue to Build source ledger and record stable source IDs, exact dated extracts, authority, freshness, relevance, version relationships, and limitations. Continue to Map claims to evidence, where each decision-bearing claim is linked to evidence and unsupported claims are exposed. Continue to Challenge supportedness and freshness. If evidence is missing, weak, stale, superseded, or outside scope, follow Missing or weak evidence back to Build source ledger and seek the named evidence or narrow the question. If every necessary claim is adequately supported, follow Supported to Answer with citations and uncertainty. The answer cites stable fixture source IDs, states the supported maintenance slot, explains why conflicting records do not control, and preserves uncertainty about matters the dossier cannot establish.
safetyNotice: FICTIONAL TRAINING FIXTURE. Alder Works, its equipment, people, records, dates, and source IDs are invented for this lesson. Fixture citations are not URLs and must not be presented as retrieved records. This component performs no retrieval, model call, scheduling action, external write, or learner-record write.

walkthroughLabel: Selected workflow stage and evidence walkthrough

sourcesIntroduction: The maintenance dossier is entirely fictional and uses internal fixture IDs rather than URLs. The external references provide background on AI risk management and retrieval-grounded generation. Neither source validates this fictional dossier or proves that a generated answer is true.

nodes.label: Question
nodes.heading: Real question or decision
nodes.description: Write the complete decision before searching. Include the target, time boundary, output needed, and the date at which the evidence must be valid.

nodes.label: Scope
nodes.heading: Bound scope and assumptions
nodes.description: Separate stated constraints from assumptions. Name what is included, what is excluded, and which changes would invalidate the answer.

nodes.label: Requirements
nodes.heading: Define evidence requirements
nodes.description: List the facts that must be established to make the decision. Specify the acceptable authority, scope, date, and precision for each fact.

nodes.label: Ledger
nodes.heading: Build source ledger
nodes.description: Record exact extracts under stable IDs. Assess authority, freshness, and relevance separately, and retain superseded or mismatched records when they explain apparent conflict.

nodes.label: Claim map
nodes.heading: Map claims to evidence
nodes.description: Break the prospective answer into checkable claims. Link each claim to evidence, record contrary evidence, and mark whether support is sufficient.

nodes.label: Challenge
nodes.heading: Challenge supportedness and freshness
nodes.description: Try to defeat the proposed answer. Check whether citations entail each claim, whether a newer version supersedes an older one, whether scope matches, and whether changed constraints require a loop or a narrower answer.

nodes.label: Answer
nodes.heading: Answer with citations and uncertainty
nodes.description: Publish only the decision the evidence supports. Cite stable source IDs at the claim level, explain resolved conflicts, and state remaining uncertainty and conditions that would change the result.

artifacts.label: FICTIONAL DECISION
artifacts.title: Full maintenance scheduling question
artifacts.body: As of 2026-09-18 at 16:00 local plant time, should fictional Alder Works schedule the four-hour bearing inspection for packaging press P-17 in North Hall during 2026-10-12 through 2026-10-16? If so, identify one continuous four-hour slot supported by the current production plan, technician roster, and shutdown authorization. Do not infer facts about other halls or weeks. If no slot is supported, say what evidence is missing or which constraint prevents a recommendation.

fields.label: Decision target
fields.value: Press P-17, North Hall

fields.label: Decision date
fields.value: Evidence valid as of 2026-09-18 16:00 local plant time

fields.label: Required output
fields.value: One supported continuous four-hour slot, or a narrow no-answer with the limiting evidence

fields.label: Not requested
fields.value: Executing a schedule change, contacting staff, or deciding maintenance for another asset

artifacts.label: SCOPE BOUNDARY
artifacts.title: Included and excluded matters
artifacts.body: The answer concerns internal maintenance scheduling only. It is not medical, legal, security, or safety certification advice. A slot must satisfy all stated constraints at once; a convenient-looking time is insufficient.

fields.label: Included
fields.value: P-17; North Hall; bearing inspection; 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-16; four continuous hours

fields.label: Excluded
fields.value: South Hall restrictions, other presses, later weeks, and any unrecorded staff availability

fields.label: As-of rule
fields.value: Use information issued by 2026-09-18 16:00. Prefer an applicable newer version when it explicitly supersedes an older one.

fields.label: Change trigger
fields.value: A later production revision, permit withdrawal, duration change, or roster change requires reassessment

artifacts.label: ASSUMPTION REGISTER
artifacts.title: What may and may not be assumed
artifacts.body: The dossier defines local times and treats the quoted records as supplied fixture evidence. It does not establish their real-world authenticity because no real organization or retrieval exists.

fields.label: Allowed fixture convention
fields.value: All times are local plant time; interval endpoints describe one continuous interval.

fields.label: Not assumed
fields.value: A technician is available outside the exact roster window.

fields.label: Not assumed
fields.value: An idle production period automatically authorizes equipment shutdown.

fields.label: Not assumed
fields.value: A rule for South Hall applies to North Hall.

fields.label: Not assumed
fields.value: A fluent answer or a citation label proves the underlying record is true.

artifacts.label: EVIDENCE PLAN
artifacts.title: Facts required before recommending a slot
artifacts.body: Each requirement is decision-bearing. Failure to establish any one prevents an unconditional recommendation.

fields.label: R1 task and duration
fields.value: Current work order or maintenance specification identifying P-17 and requiring four continuous hours.

fields.label: R2 production availability
fields.value: Current applicable North Hall production plan containing a continuous four-hour idle interval in the candidate week.

fields.label: R3 technician availability
fields.value: Current roster showing a qualified named technician available throughout that same interval.

fields.label: R4 shutdown authority
fields.value: Applicable authorization permitting P-17 shutdown throughout that same interval.

fields.label: R5 version status
fields.value: Enough version metadata to resolve any older/newer conflict without silently mixing versions.

fields.label: R6 answer precision
fields.value: Citations must support the exact date, time, asset, duration, and conditions stated.

artifacts.label: SOURCE EVALUATION
artifacts.title: Authority, freshness, and relevance are different questions
artifacts.body: Authority asks whether a source is entitled to establish the fact. Freshness asks whether it is current enough for the decision date. Relevance asks whether its asset, location, period, and subject match the claim. Strength in one dimension does not repair failure in another.

fields.label: Authority example
fields.value: A production-control plan can establish planned line availability, but not technician qualification.

fields.label: Freshness example
fields.value: An earlier plan remains a historical version but may be superseded for this decision.

fields.label: Relevance example
fields.value: A new South Hall restriction is fresh but outside the North Hall scope.

fields.label: Ledger rule
fields.value: Keep exact extracts and limitations so readers can reproduce the comparison.

artifacts.label: CLAIM/EVIDENCE MAP
artifacts.title: Main decision claims and support status
artifacts.body: The proposed recommendation is decomposed so each element can be challenged. Citations are fixture IDs pointing to exact extracts in this lesson.

fields.label: C1: task needs four continuous hours
fields.value: Supported by [AW-MNT-017]. Direct authority and scope match.

fields.label: C2: Friday 08:00–12:00 is currently idle
fields.value: Supported by [AW-PROD-204-v2]. Contrary Wednesday window in [AW-PROD-204-v1] is superseded.

fields.label: C3: qualified technician covers the full slot
fields.value: Supported by [AW-ROSTER-88], which covers 07:00–13:00 and records P-series qualification.

fields.label: C4: shutdown is authorized for the full slot
fields.value: Supported by [AW-SHUT-31], whose 07:30–12:30 window contains the proposed four hours.

fields.label: C5: South Hall restriction blocks the slot
fields.value: Not supported. [AW-SOUTH-09] is fresh but expressly limited to South Hall.

fields.label: C6: the slot is guaranteed to remain available
fields.value: Not supported. The dossier establishes a plan as of the cutoff, not a guarantee against later revisions.

fields.label: Decision status
fields.value: A conditional recommendation for Friday 2026-10-16, 08:00–12:00 is supported as of the stated cutoff.

artifacts.label: FAILURE EXAMPLE
artifacts.title: Why a fluent unsupported claim fails
artifacts.body: Unsupported draft: “The best and safest time is Wednesday 14 October from 13:00 to 17:00 because production is idle and the whole maintenance team is available.” The sentence is fluent but fails. Its Wednesday availability relies on superseded [AW-PROD-204-v1]; current [AW-PROD-204-v2] assigns production during most of that interval. No source establishes that the whole maintenance team is available, and “best” or “safest” introduces criteria the dossier never defines. Adding citations would not repair claims those citations do not entail.

fields.label: Stale support
fields.value: The Wednesday plan was explicitly superseded.

fields.label: Contradicted claim
fields.value: Current production evidence assigns an urgent order Wednesday 12:00–18:00.

fields.label: Invented fact
fields.value: No extract states that the whole maintenance team is available.

fields.label: Undefined judgment
fields.value: No comparative criterion establishes “best” or “safest.”

fields.label: Repair
fields.value: Use the supported Friday slot, state the as-of condition, and avoid unsupported superlatives.

artifacts.label: CHALLENGE CHECK
artifacts.title: Questions to ask before publishing
artifacts.body: A citation count is not a supportedness test. Challenge the relationship between each exact claim and its evidence.

fields.label: Entailment
fields.value: Does the cited extract establish the precise asset, time, duration, and condition claimed?

fields.label: Authority
fields.value: Is the issuer positioned to establish this type of fact?

fields.label: Freshness
fields.value: Was the source valid at the decision cutoff, and is a newer applicable version supplied?

fields.label: Relevance
fields.value: Do location, asset, task, and period match?

fields.label: Conflict
fields.value: Is disagreement genuine, or resolved by supersession, date, or scope?

fields.label: Completeness
fields.value: Is every necessary claim supported, or must the workflow return to the ledger?

fields.label: Change sensitivity
fields.value: Would a later revision invalidate the recommendation or require a narrower answer?

artifacts.label: FULLY WORKED FICTIONAL ANSWER
artifacts.title: Supported recommendation with traceable citations
artifacts.body: As of 2026-09-18 at 16:00 local plant time, schedule the fictional P-17 bearing inspection for Friday 2026-10-16 from 08:00 to 12:00, subject to confirming that no newer applicable revision is issued before reservation. The task requires four continuous hours and a P-series-qualified technician [AW-MNT-017]. The current North Hall production plan identifies P-17 as idle during that exact interval [AW-PROD-204-v2]. Sam Ibarra is recorded as P-series qualified and assigned to North Hall from 07:00 to 13:00, covering the proposed slot [AW-ROSTER-88]. North Hall Operations authorizes a P-17 shutdown from 07:30 to 12:30 for no more than four continuous hours, also covering the slot [AW-SHUT-31]. The older Wednesday idle window does not control because its source says it was superseded in full by version 2 [AW-PROD-204-v1; AW-PROD-204-v2]. The newer South Hall Friday restriction does not conflict because its stated scope is South Hall, not P-17 in North Hall [AW-SOUTH-09]. Uncertainty: these fictional records support a plan only at the stated cutoff. They do not guarantee that production, staffing, or authorization will remain unchanged, and this lesson has not authenticated or retrieved any real record. If an applicable later revision appears, reassess before scheduling.

fields.label: Recommended slot
fields.value: Friday 2026-10-16, 08:00–12:00 local plant time

fields.label: Why exactly four hours
fields.value: 08:00–12:00 satisfies the four-continuous-hour requirement and fits within every supplied applicable window.

fields.label: Resolved conflict
fields.value: Production v2 supersedes v1; South Hall restriction is outside North Hall scope.

fields.label: Qualification
fields.value: Conditional on no newer applicable record changing production, staffing, task duration, or shutdown authority.

fields.label: External action
fields.value: None. This rendered answer does not create or modify a maintenance schedule.

artifacts.label: TRACEABILITY CHECK
artifacts.title: Citation-to-claim audit
artifacts.body: A reader can follow each bracketed fixture ID to an exact extract in the ledger. The citations identify supplied evidence, not proof of authenticity.

fields.label: [AW-MNT-017]
fields.value: Supports asset, task, four-hour duration, candidate week, deadline, and qualification requirement.

fields.label: [AW-PROD-204-v2]
fields.value: Supports Friday 08:00–12:00 production idleness and supersession of v1.

fields.label: [AW-ROSTER-88]
fields.value: Supports Sam Ibarra's qualification record and 07:00–13:00 North Hall assignment.

fields.label: [AW-SHUT-31]
fields.value: Supports P-17 shutdown authorization from 07:30–12:30 for at most four hours.

fields.label: [AW-PROD-204-v1]
fields.value: Documents the obsolete Wednesday window and its superseded status.

fields.label: [AW-SOUTH-09]
fields.value: Supports only a South Hall restriction and therefore explains, but does not control, the scope comparison.

artifacts.label: METHOD LIMIT
artifacts.title: Grounding is not universal proof
artifacts.body: This workflow can make the relationship between an answer and supplied evidence inspectable. It cannot by itself establish that records are authentic, that the ledger is complete, that an issuer is honest, or that future conditions will remain stable. A generated claim remains unsupported when its evidence is absent, unsuitable, or non-entailing, even if the prose sounds confident.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 1, INDEPENDENT FICTIONAL CASE
artifacts.title: Missing duration evidence for mixer M-4
artifacts.body: Question: “Choose a maintenance window for mixer M-4 during the week beginning Monday 2026-10-19.” Extract [PX-M4-REQ], issued 2026-09-18 by Maintenance Intake: “Inspect M-4 during the week of 19 October. Duration to be confirmed after engineering review.” Extract [PX-M4-PROD], issued 2026-09-18 by Production Control: “M-4 idle Tuesday 09:00–12:00.” Extract [PX-M4-ROSTER], issued 2026-09-18 by Staffing: “Qualified technician Lee available Tuesday 09:00–12:00.” No engineering duration record or shutdown authorization is supplied.

fields.label: Known
fields.value: A three-hour idle interval and technician availability are supplied.

fields.label: Missing
fields.value: What additional evidence, if any, must be established before a specific slot can be supported?

fields.label: Decision consequence
fields.value: Using the extracts, decide whether a specific slot is supportable and explain which claims the evidence does or does not establish.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 2, INDEPENDENT FICTIONAL CASE
artifacts.title: Apparent conflict resolved by version and scope
artifacts.body: Question: “Is compressor C-2 in East Hall available for inspection on Thursday 2026-10-22 from 10:00–12:00?” [PX-C2-v1], East Hall Production, 2026-09-01: “C-2 runs Thursday 10:00–12:00.” [PX-C2-v2], East Hall Production, 2026-09-19: “Supersedes PX-C2-v1. C-2 idle Thursday 10:00–12:00.” [PX-WEST-5], Facilities, 2026-09-20: “West Hall compressors may not stop Thursday.” [PX-C2-PERMIT], East Hall Operations, 2026-09-19: “C-2 inspection shutdown authorized Thursday 10:00–12:00.”

fields.label: Version relationship
fields.value: Compare the supplied versions and state how their dates and any supersession language affect which record controls.

fields.label: Scope relationship
fields.value: Compare the location and asset named in each extract with the decision target.

fields.label: Supported conclusion
fields.value: Based only on the supplied extracts, state whether the requested interval is supportable and explain your reasoning.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 3, INDEPENDENT FICTIONAL CASE
artifacts.title: Changed constraint after an earlier answer
artifacts.body: An earlier answer recommended pump P-9 maintenance on Monday 2026-10-26 from 08:00–11:00 using [PX-P9-PROD] and [PX-P9-PERMIT-v1]. New extract [PX-P9-PERMIT-v2], issued 2026-09-20 by Operations: “Supersedes PX-P9-PERMIT-v1. Monday P-9 shutdown authorization is withdrawn because the isolation test is incomplete. No replacement window is authorized.” The question is re-asked as of 2026-09-21. No completed isolation test, replacement permit, or alternative production and staffing window is supplied.

fields.label: Changed fact
fields.value: The authorization supporting the earlier slot has been explicitly withdrawn.

fields.label: Current evidence
fields.value: No replacement authorization or fully evidenced alternative slot is supplied.

fields.label: Supported response boundary
fields.value: Using the changed record and the evidence supplied, determine the narrowest response that is justified and identify any evidence needed for a replacement recommendation.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 1 EXPLANATION
artifacts.title: Why missing evidence returns to the ledger
artifacts.body: The three-hour production and roster overlap cannot establish a viable window when task duration is expressly unconfirmed and shutdown permission is absent. The supported action is to return to the ledger for an engineering duration record and applicable shutdown authorization, or narrow the answer to “no supported slot yet.”

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 2 EXPLANATION
artifacts.title: Why this apparent conflict is resolved
artifacts.body: The newer East Hall plan explicitly supersedes the older one, so the old running schedule is historical rather than controlling. The West Hall restriction is outside the asset's East Hall scope. The current applicable plan and permit support the stated interval within this fictional dossier.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 3 EXPLANATION
artifacts.title: Why changed constraints require a narrow answer
artifacts.body: The newer permit removes a necessary condition for the earlier recommendation and supplies no replacement. Repeating the old answer would be stale, while inventing another window would lack production, staffing, and authorization support. The justified answer is to withdraw the recommendation and request a current permit plus evidence for any proposed alternative.

choices.label: Return to the source ledger and request the engineering duration plus applicable shutdown authorization; do not name a slot yet.
choices.announcement: Practice 1 is correct. Missing decision-bearing evidence returns the workflow to the source ledger.
choices.feedback: Correct. Production idleness and technician availability do not establish how long the task takes or whether shutdown is authorized. Naming Tuesday 09:00–12:00 would guess two necessary facts, so the workflow must loop to the ledger or issue a narrow no-slot answer.

choices.label: Recommend Tuesday 09:00–12:00 because production and a technician are both available for three hours.
choices.announcement: Practice 1 needs another attempt. The duration and shutdown authority are missing.
choices.feedback: Not supported. The request says duration is still to be confirmed, and no shutdown authorization is supplied. An overlapping idle and roster interval cannot fill either gap.

choices.label: Treat all four extracts as equally controlling and refuse to answer because they mention incompatible schedules or halls.
choices.announcement: Practice 2 needs another attempt. Compare version status and scope rather than counting disagreement.
choices.feedback: Not supported. PX-C2-v2 explicitly supersedes v1, resolving the date conflict. PX-WEST-5 applies to West Hall, not C-2 in East Hall. Treating every mention as equally applicable ignores both version and scope.

choices.label: Use PX-C2-v2 and PX-C2-PERMIT for East Hall; explain that v1 is superseded and the West Hall restriction is out of scope.
choices.announcement: Practice 2 is correct. Version and scope resolve the apparent conflict.
choices.feedback: Correct. The newer applicable production plan replaces the older plan, and the newer West Hall rule is irrelevant to the East Hall asset. The current East Hall plan and permit support the two-hour interval.

choices.label: Repeat the earlier Monday recommendation because it was supported when first written.
choices.announcement: Practice 3 needs another attempt. A newer applicable constraint invalidates the earlier recommendation.
choices.feedback: Not supported. PX-P9-PERMIT-v2 explicitly withdraws the authorization required by the old answer. Prior support does not make an answer timeless, and no evidence supports an alternative slot.

choices.label: Withdraw the earlier slot and state that no new slot is supported until a current authorization and matching availability evidence are supplied.
choices.announcement: Practice 3 is correct. The changed constraint requires a narrow answer rather than a guessed replacement.
choices.feedback: Correct. The new permit version defeats a necessary claim in the earlier answer. Because no replacement authorization or complete alternative dossier exists, abstaining from a new slot is the only supported decision.
